Step into the Octagon UFC fighting

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Its a world very few get to witness - Mixed Martial Arts fight camps .We join two of the best UFC fighters South Africa has produced to date, join us as we go into fight camp and they prepare fo

Unique Selling Point:
Background
It’s an Iconic moment in South African sporting history: Its UFC 282 ( 2022)…. The glitz and glam of Las Vegas coupled with the imposing, boisterous T- Mobile Arena packed with tens of thousands of spectators baying for blood would be enough to send chills down the spine of even the most hardened of fighters…
In the shadows of the arena a hulking figure can be seen pacing up and down, draped in a colourful South African Flag…he kisses it and says a short prayer, like a gladiator making peace with whatever the Gods might have in store. Its time, his name is called: “Hailing from South Africa, with a record of 18 – 2 in the middleweight division…Dricus ‘Stillknocks’ Du Plessis” !!!
In his second appearance of the year, Du Plessis took on former welterweight title challenger Darren Till on the main card of UFC 282 at T-Mobile Arena, in what would be a bout to remember, with the 28-year-old dominating the opening round before Englishman Till bounced back in the second. Du Plessis, though, got a second wind in the final round and locked up a submission after securing a takedown…Sending a stern warning to elite fighters like Israel Adesanya and Alex Parreira…
But South Africa’s amazing showing at UFC 282 was made the more sweeter when Dricus’s understudy, 21 Year old Pretoria born Cameron Saaiman stole the show with a dominant display Cameron earlier rallied from getting a point deducted in the second round of his fight against Steven Kozlow,unleashing a barrage of strikes on Kozlow to hand him the first stoppage and first loss of his career. Saaiman improved to 7-0 with his TKO victory and to cap off his win UFC president Dana White labelling Cameron as the future of the UFC.
And now the two are preparing to take on UFC 285…Where Dricus will be facing 5th ranked Derek Brunson who has been described as “A straight up Killer”,with incredible striking power,a win against Brunson would catapult him to a position where he could challenge the current champion Alex Pereirra.
Whilst Dricus takes on the elite of UFC Cameron will be looking to make an even bigger impression as he takes on 28-year-old American Jonathan Martinez.

As the fighters prepare to take on UFC 285, Carte Blanche has been invited to join the pair as they go into fight camp… This is a privilege, as usually fight camps are closed off ,with no cameras allowed. This is a rare occasion where will get insight into what it takes to prepare for an enormous even like this, We will have access to all the techniques used in preparation for a UFC bout, we will have access to the fighter’s daily routines , sparing session and all the coaching staff. This piece will also seek to go beyon the octagon and will delve into the lives of these usually recluse athletes, where we will meet the people who have gotten them to their now elite level.


Summary:
My aim is to make this an exciting , high octane piece which gives a rare insight into the world of MMA. It will follow out two protagonists who are on a journey to be at the top of the MMA world, but you don’t just get there , this takes guts , determination and a whole lot of broken ribs and black eyes. I want to delve deep into what makes them tip, and what is the driving force behind their success. I also aim to disprove the notion that MMA is a sport for brutes and ignorant people. I want to showcase this journey in the most honest and raw manner …so strap on , there will be blood,

Further information:
UFC to come to Africa and South Africa ?

This has now become a multibillion dollar industry, with millions of fans around the world,gone are the days where many sporting fans considered Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) a sport for bloodthirsty bruts,but has a huge following-especially amongst young people.Superstars like Conor Macgregor, Israel Adesanya and Jon Jones have become cult heroes.
Following UFC 279- last year, president Dana White stated that the UFC is in serious talks to bring an event to the continent.
Bringing the promotion to Africa and South Africa has been a topic of a discussion for quite some time. White has stated in the past it was something he wants to accomplish by the end of 2023. The story will look into growing the sport in South Africa and the rest of the continent.
The UFC has never hosted an event in Africa. In recent years, the African talent on the UFC roster has grown significantly. There has been three UFC champions from Africa: Israel Adesanya (Nigeria) ,Francis Ngannou (Cameroon) and Kamaru Usman ( Nigeria).Dricus and Cameron are looking to join their ranks and judging from word in and out of the Octagon … South Africa will soon have have a UFC champion of its own.

Treatment :
Opening sequence: Open with powerful visuals of Dricus and Cameron from UFC 282 Match.
I would like to start the piece with what I think was such a powerful moment of UFC 282 : We see Dricus Du Plessis in the shadows clutching the South African Flag, the spotlight is on him , he drapes the flag on his shoulder, as the crowd is cheering…The visuals are in slow motion… we cut to a tracking shot of Dricus moving through the crowd with the South African Flag [We hear the commentator speaking over the noise of the crowd: “The South African Dricus du Plessis wants to show what South African Martial Arts has to show, a proud moment”] -
We see Dricus walk into the octagon and starts pacing and shadow boxing …We hear Dricus’s voice over the visuals: [“When I step into that ring nothing matters... I am there to represent my nation, my family and everyone] we Fast cut to Dricus knocking down an opponent, the visuals cut to Cameron Saaiman in slow motion landing punches on an opponent [We hear the commentator shouting “ow what a punch by Cameron Saaiman], we see more punch combinations from Cameron, as his voice can be heard over the visuals :[ There is nothing like being in that ring ,I wanted to make my country proud, I have been waiting for that moment]
We dip to black as we see slow more visuals of Dricus and Cameron lifting their arms in victory with the UFC commentator speaking over the visuals [UFC 282 Wow…South Africa is officially on the map now”]. We dip to black.
My aim is to make this an exciting , high octane piece which gives a rare insight into the world of MMA. It will follow out two protagonists who are on a journey to be at the top of the MMA world, but you don’t just get there , this takes guts , determination and a whole lot of broken ribs and black eyes. I want to delve deep into what makes them tip, and what is the driving force behind their success. I also aim to disprove the notion that MMA is a sport for brutes and ignorant people. I want to showcase this journey in the most honest and raw manner …so strap on , there will be blood, there will be nauseating knockouts and it will be loud and we’ll likely grade some footage just to make it grungy.
The idea is to have the presenter dressed in his training gear ready for a day at fight camp. Training with elite fighters Drikus Du Plessis and Camerson Saaiman.
Presenter link (2 locations depending on what’s possible)
• Location 1: Pretoria with Dricus at the end of a morning run (ideally at sunrise 05.30) the two run up to the top of a staircase – dramatic Rocky Balboa moment.
• Location 2: Westcliff stairs same link, just without Drikus. Presenter intro to MMA and what MMA fighting is / what does it take to be an elite MMA fighter
Interviews:
1. Dricus at Home
We are at Discus’s house in Hatfield, Pretoria. Its dark outside, presenter does a link in the car – going in to fetch him for their run. Drikus is also in his training gear, Dricus walks out pulls his hoodie over his head, [I want the shot to be handheld, not to polished]. He looks at his fitbit, him and presenter meet on the curb and.. we’re off!!!
2. Cameron Saaimon
Another early morning (drive the idea of how much dedication is required for this sport), meeting Cameron at the gym. Underground parking, we see the empty parking.. we don’t yet make it clear where we are – presenter link: ‘Another early morning.. I’m not built for this, today’s elite fighter Cameron Saiimon…. We see his car drive into the lot. He’s in his training gear, walks out the car and invites presenter to come open the gym with him for his session.
Transition into fast paced action visuals of Dricus pummelling opponents, and cut to visuals of Dricus in training …We move into sit down interview with Dricus , where he speaks about how he started out at the age of 5…
3. Drikus’ parents (How he started out….and how he dropped out of varsity to pursue his dream of being an MMA champion.) In person at their home in PTA

4. Cameron Saaimon’s parents (ZOOM as they’re in CT) we also have his sister she would be an in person interview in Pretoria

5. Couch Morne Visser (Couch to both the guys) in person at the gym

6. Dr Danella Eliasov
We transition with visuals of Dricus and Coach Morne Visser correcting Cameron’s fighting stance [This is one of fighting aspects they have been working on]. We see beautiful slow- motion highlight visuals of Cameron knocking an opponent out. We cut to visuals of UFC president Dana White stating that “Cameron Saaiman is the future and that should be his new fight name.”


We cut to slow-mo visuals of Cameron sparring , we see the seat dripping from his face, we can see the determination in his eyes [ Under the visuals we hear Cameron speak about his love for MMA and what it feels like to be in the Octagon]- we then transition to the sit down interview with the presenter.
Link : We see walking in the octagon as fighter spar in the background …We are on a tracking shot which goes outside the octagon and meets our producer on a MCU.[ Link on the fact that both Dricus and Cameron are at the elite level of the UFC.]
We see coach Morne taking the boys through their paces, he is shouting and cursing at the fighter [ That is his character, but we see the guys chirping back and smiling], We hard cut to our interview with him. This will be a standing interview. He speaks on his fighters , the family they have created and how brutal the fight camp is.

Script:


Step into the Octagon

Opening sequence: Path to the stars (music site: Mamadance .)

Upsound Dricus: 00:37:18:28 When I make that walk, it's game time.

Upsound Dricus : 00:35:14:28 it's a very honest moment in anybody's life. There's no excuse.

Upsound Cameron 1:55 The first round starts, and it's dead quiet….no one wants to miss a second of the fight.

Upsound Cameron, it's a game of inches…you can get knocked out…you can get choked out…you can get taken down.

Upsound Dricus: 00:37:52:26 you must have the mindset that I might get killed … the hardest part is do you have what it takes to kill as well?

[Fade out of black]
Link opening Derek: Once thought of as just a violent and bloody activitt, relegated to the fringes of society, Mixed Martial Arts has erupted as a major spectator sport around the world.

1 V/O: And its biggest platform is the Ultimate fighting championship or UFC. Worth a mere 2 million dollars in 2001, it’s now valued at a massive 7 billion dollars.

2 V/O: Broadcast to billions in over 160 countries, the UFC stages fights in an Octagon - its best exponents becoming global superstars.

3 V/O: And two South Africans are among them.


4 V/O: On an early weekend morning in Pretoria, we’re joining Dricus Du Plessis and Cameron Saaiman at a fight camp as they prepare for a UFC event in the United States next month. It offers a rare glimpse of the fighting coal-face.

Upsound Derek : I was going to take on Dricus and Cameron at the same time ,but I’ve got a bad cold

5 V/O: Fight camps are brutal, pushing fighters to their physical and mental limits.


Upsound Morne Visser: 00:03:04:12 - 00:03:21:05 if you walk into this door, you must want to be a world champion. Otherwise, I'm not interested.

6 V/O: Morne Visser is a top MMA coach, determined to take both Dricus and Cameron to the top of the UFC. This camp is a vital part of getting there.

Upsound Derek: 00:29:19:23 Have you got a senior’s division?
Upsound Coach Morne Visser 00:29:31:22 - 00:30:02:25: Fight camp for us is 12 weeks. Two weeks before the fight, We go the double distance. Dricus will be in the cage for double the time and every minute a fresh guy comes in and all my guys are high calibre guys, so I mean you've got ten guys waiting to just have a minute with him to break him.
Upsound Dricus: 00:03:48:01 - 00:04:18:06 This sport . would say it's a little bit of an obsession - just to have one fight.
8 V/O: It’s an obsession that revealed itself early in Dricus’s life. By 14 he was hard at training and by 18 a world kickboxing champion. Then, as a student, opportunity knocked on Africa’s biggest mixed martial arts stage, the Extreme Fighting Championship or EFC.
Upsound Dricus du Plessis 00:07:13:11 - 00:07:47:10 I had six months left to finish my degree. And I got a title shot and I told my dad, Listen, I have one shot at this.
00:07:47:12 If I lose that fight, I'd go back to studying.
NEW V/O: A younger and leaner Dricus took to the African octagon for a fight that would define his future.

00:07:47:? I won that fight and I became the youngest champion in the EFC and the rest is history.
9 V/O For this champ the UFC beckoned.
[Visuals Cameron sparring]
10 V/O His protege, Cameron, is six years Dricus’s junior - but already making waves.
Upsound Cameron: 0:29 My love for MMA started when I was 10 years old. That was the first time I actually went to go watch EFC events.
Upsound Cameron: 12:56 at the age of 17, for k I transitioned into MMA and won amateur titles. When that happened, I really thought okay, we can make this work.
11 V/O: Making it work means making it big in the UFC. First, though, and like Dricus, Cameron needed to prove himself in Africa’s EFC.
12 V/O: In 2021 he did precisely that: winning the Bantamweight title aged just 21 from the more experienced, Sindile Manengela.
Upsound Morne Visser 00:10:27:11 You must remember everybody wants to be at the top, and that's the UFC .Dricus because he had to be a two times champion in the EFC before they even looked at him.

NEW V/O If the EFC title fight had been career defining, his first foray into the multi-million dollar international big time was make-or-break. UPS He was matched against 7-year UFC veteran, Markus Perez, from Brazil.
Upsound Dricus Du Plessis 00:13:41:15 - 00:14:19:27 When I finally got to the UFC, first fight, first second of that first fight, I could immediately feel this is step up. Now I'm fighting the best in the world right now.
NEW V/O Dricus won by knockout and - going into the Las Vegas event now the 10th ranked middleweight in the UFC . His success might just have helped Cameron clinch a sought after spot at the sport’s global showcase, too.
Upsound Morne Visser: 00:10:57:25 - 00:11:19:07 Cammy We got a lucky break because the UFC saw in Dricus we've got a different breed of fighter.

NEW V/O The UFC isn’t open to just anyone. You need to be special, and you need to be invited. Cameron hoped his EFC Bantamweight title victory would clinch a deal.
Upsound Cameron Saaiman 28:58: my manager at that time sent that footage to the matchmakers at the UFC .. And in August of last year, we got the shots and we made it happen.

NEW V/O: In his full UFC debut, he fought a specialist in the Ju Jitsu martial art, the American, Steven Koslow.

New V/O: Four months previously, the UFC’s owner had described Cameron as “The Future”. This win by technical knockout indicates that might just be true.

Upsound Dricus: I get more nervous when Cameron fights than myself
Upsound Cameron: Dricus has always been there. he was there to emotionally support me through a lot of things
FIGHT CAMP VISUALS WITH NOISE FOR THE SCENE CHANGE
14 V/O:In Vegas, Dricus will be fighting American Derek Brunson, a wrestling specialist with a fearsome reputation.
[visuals of wrestling and take down and then Derek Brunson]
Upsound Derek 00:16:29:09 - 00:16:31:07: Do you watch Derek's tapes?
Upsound Dricus Du Plessis 00:16:31:09 - 00:16:51:05 Absolutely. Absolutely. I trained with him - I've gone to training in America. And I know exactly how he fights. And he's a brilliant fighter. He's not number five in the world for nothing. And I think we have all the tools necessary to beat this guy.
Upsound Coach Morne00:12:39:14 - I believe the Brunson fight, definitely don't put your money on anything else but a finish and a fight bonus.
[beat, visuals of Cameron boxing]
15 V/O On the same night Cameron will be facing another American: seasoned fighter Jonathan Martinez
Upsound Cameron 1:57 We have amazing training partners, there are movement patterns my opponent does , when they watch footage they try to do that and that’s how we prepare.
16 V/O: Question is: were they prepared for me?
Upsound Dricus 0:49:49:07 It doesn't sound good. No. And the name is very applicable.
Upsound Derek 0:49:52:12 - But could you demonstrate it to me gently?
Upsound Dricus 00:49:54:29 I can do that for you.
17 V/O: It took just a few seconds to realise fight camp wasn’t for me. For these two elite fighters, though, another two weeks of blood and sweat awaits.



[end]

It offers a rare glimpse of the fighting coal-face. Upsound Derek : I was going to take on Dricus and Cameron at the same time ,but I’ve got a bad cold 5 V/O: Fight camps are brutal, pushing fighters to their physical and mental limits. metadata.Unique Selling Point: Background It’s an Iconic moment in South African sporting history: Its UFC 282 ( 2022)…. The glitz and glam of Las Vegas coupled with the imposing, boisterous T- Mobile Arena packed with tens of thousands of spectators baying for blood would be enough to send chills down the spine of even the most hardened of fighters… In the shadows of the arena a hulking figure can be seen pacing up and down, draped in a colourful South African Flag…he kisses it and says a short prayer, like a gladiator making peace with whatever the Gods might have in store. Its time, his name is called: “Hailing from South Africa, with a record of 18 – 2 in the middleweight division…Dricus ‘Stillknocks’ Du Plessis” !!! In his second appearance of the year, Du Plessis took on former welterweight title challenger Darren Till on the main card of UFC 282 at T-Mobile Arena, in what would be a bout to remember, with the 28-year-old dominating the opening round before Englishman Till bounced back in the second. Du Plessis, though, got a second wind in the final round and locked up a submission after securing a takedown…Sending a stern warning to elite fighters like Israel Adesanya and Alex Parreira… But South Africa’s amazing showing at UFC 282 was made the more sweeter when Dricus’s understudy, 21 Year old Pretoria born Cameron Saaiman stole the show with a dominant display Cameron earlier rallied from getting a point deducted in the second round of his fight against Steven Kozlow,unleashing a barrage of strikes on Kozlow to hand him the first stoppage and first loss of his career. Saaiman improved to 7-0 with his TKO victory and to cap off his win UFC president Dana White labelling Cameron as the future of the UFC. And now the two are preparing to take on UFC 285…Where Dricus will be facing 5th ranked Derek Brunson who has been described as “A straight up Killer”,with incredible striking power,a win against Brunson would catapult him to a position where he could challenge the current champion Alex Pereirra. Whilst Dricus takes on the elite of UFC Cameron will be looking to make an even bigger impression as he takes on 28-year-old American Jonathan Martinez. As the fighters prepare to take on UFC 285, Carte Blanche has been invited to join the pair as they go into fight camp… This is a privilege, as usually fight camps are closed off ,with no cameras allowed. This is a rare occasion where will get insight into what it takes to prepare for an enormous even like this, We will have access to all the techniques used in preparation for a UFC bout, we will have access to the fighter’s daily routines , sparing session and all the coaching staff. This piece will also seek to go beyon the octagon and will delve into the lives of these usually recluse athletes, where we will meet the people who have gotten them to their now elite level.

I want to delve deep into what makes them tip, and what is the driving force behind their success. I also aim to disprove the notion that MMA is a sport for brutes and ignorant people. I want to showcase this journey in the most honest and raw manner …so strap on , there will be blood,
metadata.Further information: UFC to come to Africa and South Africa ? This has now become a multibillion dollar industry, with millions of fans around the world,gone are the days where many sporting fans considered Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) a sport for bloodthirsty bruts,but has a huge following-especially amongst young people.Superstars like Conor Macgregor, Israel Adesanya and Jon Jones have become cult heroes. Following UFC 279- last year, president Dana White stated that the UFC is in serious talks to bring an event to the continent. Bringing the promotion to Africa and South Africa has been a topic of a discussion for quite some time. White has stated in the past it was something he wants to accomplish by the end of 2023. The story will look into growing the sport in South Africa and the rest of the continent. The UFC has never hosted an event in Africa. In recent years, the African talent on the UFC roster has grown significantly. There has been three UFC champions from Africa: Israel Adesanya (Nigeria) ,Francis Ngannou (Cameroon) and Kamaru Usman ( Nigeria).Dricus and Cameron are looking to join their ranks and judging from word in and out of the Octagon … South Africa will soon have have a UFC champion of its own.
